_doc: The post: courier houses based in towns (systems/couriers.js, state on world.post) and the letters the player sends through them (systems/mail.js, state on player.mail). A courier house has an owner (an NPC or the player), stations (towns it serves), riders, relay horses, guards, a speed tier, a postage price, a reputation and cash. Each week every town writes letters (demand from its size and its court), split among the couriers with a station there by price, speed and reputation; wages, horses and stations are paid; riders on dangerous roads (war, raiders, outlaw lairs) are robbed. NPC houses are founded where a town goes unserved, open stations when rich, cut prices when losing and go bankrupt. A crown may grant one house a Royal Post charter: only it carries that realm's mail. The player's letters travel real days by distance, roads and season, and may be lost, delayed, robbed or intercepted; the recipient's answer comes back to Journal -> Letters.

mail._voice: Letters in their writers' voices (systems/mailVoice.js; grammar in letters below) and what mail.js lets them carry. Unbidden letters: from firstDay, one every gap days at most from a correspondent (written to before, or a spouse or governing companion away) whose regard is at least minRegard, maxPending on the road at once; family news (a death, a birth, a wedding, a crown) brings up to eventMax letters within eventDays. Hooks: a plea for food from a town in want (requestChance, once per requestDays; requestQty units or 1.5x their price in gold), an invitation to visit (inviteChance, once per inviteDays, inviteDeadline days to come; kept: visit* goodwill, missed: missedVisit), a lord's steward's feast invitation (feastChance), a tip about a rival House's agent in their town (tipChance, +tipSuspicion) or an outlaw lair near it (lairTipChance), a court scandal's truth (secretChance), coin from their purse (coinChance), goods bought in their market (goodsChance), a keepsake from a spouse or love (tokenChance).

_riders: Riders on the map (systems/courierRiders.js; the game's own day only, never the headless harness): each letter the player sends from the Letters panel rides as a 'courier_rider' unit along the road, due at the recipient's town on the letter's arrival day. A sample of the houses' traffic rides too: every everyDays days a house may send one rider (npcChance, at most npcPerHouse) between two stations when an end is within nearRange of the player, at most npcMax on the map; the player's own house sends up to ownHouseMax (ownHouseChance), shown even in the fog. On the road: a raider band or lair beast within hostileRange robs with chance its strength / (its strength + the rider's guards) x robShare; an active outlaw lair within lairRange with lairChance x (1 - guard cover); a realm at war with the recipient's realm reads a lord's, rival's or child's letter (warIntercept) or seizes a house rider's bag (warSeize). Guards: guardBase + guard cover x guardPer. Bags: bagLetters, bagGold coin, a lord's sealed letter (sealedChance). Robbed by the player: Underworld crime robbery.crime (data/underworld.json), robbery.reputation lost in the realm, the house's reputation -robbery.houseRep, a sealed letter to the inbox (courtLetters stolen_mailbag) worth robbery.sealedPrice to the lord's enemy.

courtesy.name: Courtesy & news
courtesy.desc: Compliments, news, a word to keep the friendship warm. Helps a little, and less each time you write the same person.
courtesy.subject: A letter of courtesy
courtesy.warm: {to} writes back warmly and thanks you for your news.
courtesy.hostile: {to} sends your letter back unopened in all but name: a single cold line.
courtesy.tiresome: {to} has had a great many letters from you lately, and the reply is short.

gift.name: A gift enclosed
gift.desc: Enclose gold or one of your goods. Riders are robbed on bad roads: what is stolen never arrives.
gift.subject: A gift, with your compliments
gift.warm: {to} thanks you handsomely for the gift.
gift.cool: {to} accepts the gift without much warmth.
gift.hostile: {to} keeps the gift and the grudge both.
gift.stolen: {to} writes that your letter came with its seal cut and nothing inside it.

favour.name: Ask a favour
favour.desc: Ask for help: a purse, an introduction, a good word. Only friends say yes, and asking costs a little goodwill. Once in a while per person. A companion away: ask them to come back to your company (those who still approve of you come; a governor hands over their post).
favour.subject: A favour asked
favour.cool: {to} regrets that they cannot help you at present.
favour.tiresome: {to} reminds you that you asked a favour only lately.

proposal.name: A proposal
proposal.desc: Lords: a pact of friendship (an alliance if you rule a realm). Rival Houses: a truce. A love: marriage. A merchant house: partnership.
proposal.subject: A proposal
proposal.cool: {to} will think on it, which is to say no.
proposal.hostile: {to} laughs at your proposal, and makes sure others hear of it.

apology.name: An apology
apology.desc: Make amends. Softens a grudge; does nothing where there is no grudge.
apology.subject: An apology
apology.cool: {to} notes your apology. The wound is not healed.
apology.puzzled: {to} writes back, puzzled: there was nothing to forgive.

threat.name: A threat or demand
threat.desc: Demand gold or obedience. The weak sometimes pay; everyone remembers. A threat that falls into an enemy's hands may please them.
threat.subject: A demand
threat.hostile: {to} answers your threat with one of their own.

love.name: A love letter
love.desc: Sweet words for a love or your spouse. If you are married and it is not to your spouse, an opened letter becomes a scandal.
love.subject: A letter of the heart
love.warm: {to} writes back with a pressed flower and more than a few kind words.
love.cool: {to} is touched, but careful in reply.
love.hostile: {to} asks you not to write such things again.

ransom.name: Negotiate a release
ransom.desc: Open talks for a child held as a hostage at that court: they name their price, or let the child go for friendship's sake.
ransom.subject: Concerning {child}
ransom.hostile: {to} names a hard price for {child}'s release.

warning.name: A warning or intelligence
warning.desc: Warn a lord of their enemy's strength. Valued, unless the enemy's spies read it first. A companion away: a word of danger about their road or their post, and they think the better of you.
warning.subject: A warning
warning.cool: {to} thanks you, though they knew most of it.

free.name: A letter in your own words
free.desc: Write what you like. They answer in their own voice (the AI brain), and the answer can carry real weight: goodwill or a grudge, a promise held, coin from their own purse, a meeting agreed. With the AI brain off it is read as the nearest plain kind of letter. Tuning: data/letterChat.json (systems/letterChat.js).
free.subject: A letter

letters._doc: The grammar replies and unprompted letters are written from (systems/mailVoice.js). Every list holds lines: a string, or { t, r, p, tone, rank, rel, type, when, not, w }. r: the writer's register or group (high: lords, rival Houses, merchant houses; trade: merchant houses; low: townsfolk and friends; kin: spouse and children; comrade: companions away). p: personas (formal, blunt, flowery, pious, sly, nervous, warm) — a line tagged with the writer's persona is three times as likely, one tagged with another is never drawn. tone: warm/cool/hostile. rank: how the player stands (crown, noble, common). rel: spouse/child/love/friend/comrade/none. type: the writer's recipient type. when/not: flags (first, again, often, reply, unprompted, old, scribe, mouth, delayed). A line whose {placeholders} the facts can't fill is never drawn. facts[k] are told only when true where the writer lives; k_still / k_over continue a thread an earlier letter began.

salutations.t: Your Majesty, begging your pardon for the liberty,

openings.t: Your letter from {fromPlace} reached me after {daysWord} on the road.
Your letter came to {town} {daysWord} after you wrote it.
Your letter from {fromPlace} came safe to my hand.
We have received your letter, written at {fromPlace}.
Your letter found us at {town}, and was read aloud before the whole court, as befits it.
Your letter was put into my hand at {town}; I have read it with attention.
Your letter is come. I will answer it as plainly as you wrote it.
The rider brought your letter, and I have read it twice over.
Got your letter.
{scribe} read me your letter at my own table, and I made {scribe} read it again.
{scribe} has read me your letter, and now sets down what I say, so forgive the plainness.
Your letter came and was read out to me, and to half the street besides.
Your letter was held up somewhere on the road, but it came at last.
Your letter came — late, the roads being what they are, but it came.
Another letter from you, and it is only {lastAgo} since the last.
It is {lastAgo} since I last had a letter from you, and here is another.
This is the {count} letter between us, and I keep every one in the chest by the bed.
You write often. A {sir} might begin to wonder why.
Your letters come thick as autumn leaves, {sir}.
Forgive me for answering late: your letter took {daysWord} to come, and I have been all at sixes and sevens since.
Your letter came safe, the gods be thanked for the roads and the rider both.
Your letter came, and I read it by the window until the light went.
Your letter came all the way to {town}, and I could not stop smiling.
Your letter reached me at {town}. I read it twice, once for the news and once for your hand.
Your letter arrived.
I have your letter. I had hoped for a better one.
Your rider waited at the gate for an answer. Here it is.
Your letter is here, and so, it seems, is the rest of your news.
You do write, I'll give you that.
I had scarcely folded your last letter away when this one came.
Your rider found me at {town} and would not leave the kitchen until I had written back.
Your letter came on a grey day and made it less so.
We have your letter of the {daysWord} past, and answer it now.
Your messenger has been fed and rested, and carries this back to you.
Your letter reached us at {town} in good order, its seal whole.
Your letter came. I read it at the well, and then again at home.
It was good to see your hand again.
Your letters keep finding me, wherever I go.

warm.t: It was good to hear from you, and better to know you think of {town}.
You are kind to remember us, and kinder to say so in ink.
We take your courtesy in the spirit it was sent, and return it gladly.
Your words were a gift in themselves; I had them read twice at supper, and the second time the whole hall fell quiet to listen.
A kind letter is a rarer thing than a rich one. I thank you for it.
Your news was welcome, and so is the friendship behind it — though I wonder what you will want of me next.
Thank you for writing. I don't get many letters, and none so kind.
Your letter warmed the house better than the fire does.
Good to have your news. Keep writing.
I am glad of your letter. The house is too quiet without you.
Your news is all over the house — the servants want to know everything.
The road has not changed you, I see; your letters are as long-winded as your stories.
Your letter came at the right time; I needed a friendly word.
What a long letter! I read every word, even the boring ones.
It is a rare pleasure to hear from someone who wants nothing.
Your letter was passed round the hall and came back to me with a wine stain on it.

cool.t: I acknowledge your letter, and your good wishes.
Your courtesy is noted.
Thank you for your letter. I am not sure what you mean by it, but thank you.
Your letter came. I have little to say in answer.
We are obliged for your letter, though our affairs leave little room for correspondence.
You are kind to write. I will be honest and say I did not expect it.
Your letter came. I have read it.
Thank you for your letter. Things are as they are here.
Your letter is kind. I hardly know what to answer.
Your news came. Mine is soon told.
We note your letter, and your continued interest in our affairs.
I read your letter. I am still deciding what I think of you.

hostile.t: I have no need of your compliments, and less of your friendship.
Spare your ink. Courtesy from you is a dagger with a ribbon tied on it.
You will forgive me if I do not pretend to be glad.
Don't write to me again.
We are not friends, whatever your letter says.

tiresome.t: You have written a great many letters to me of late, and I have answered a great many. This answer will be short.
A great many letters from you lately — the rider knows the way better than I do. I have little new to say.
Your letters come faster than I can answer them, {sir}. A great many letters say less than a few.
So many letters! A great many letters, and I have nothing new to put in mine.

child.t: I miss home more than I can say, and your letter made me miss it more.
Thank you for your letter. I have read it so often the creases are coming through.
I am well, and doing my duty here as you taught me.

warm.t: Thank you for {gift}. It was more than generous.
Bless you for {gift}. I have never had such a thing come by letter.
We have received {gift} and thank you for it handsomely; our steward has put it where it will do most good.
{gift} came safe with your letter. A gift like that is not forgotten.
{gift}! You are a dear, foolish, generous thing, and I am keeping every bit of it.
{gift} came with your letter, and I wept a little, which you are not to tell anyone.
Thank you for {gift}. I shall find a use for it — and remember who sent it.
{gift}, by the gods! I lit a candle at the shrine for you the same day.
Thank you for {gift}. I'll not pretend it isn't needed.
{gift} — you remembered. The lads were jealous.
{gift} came safe. The whole street knew of it by evening — you cannot keep a secret in {town}.
I have {gift} in a jar by the hearth, and I look at it more than I should.
{gift} reached us intact, which says something for your rider and more for your generosity.
Our thanks for {gift}. Such tokens bind friends more surely than oaths.
{gift}. Well. I won't pretend I didn't need it.

cool.t: {gift} arrived with your letter. I thank you for it.
We acknowledge {gift}. Gifts are easily sent; we will see what follows.
Thank you for {gift}. I hope it does not come with strings.
{gift} came. I will keep it, since you sent it.
{gift} came with your letter. I hardly know what I have done to deserve it.
{gift} is noted in our books.

hostile.t: {gift} came. I have kept it, and the grudge besides.
You think {gift} buys you back into my good graces? It buys you this letter, and no more.
We have received {gift}. Do not mistake our accepting it for forgiveness.

stolen.t: Your letter came with its seal cut and nothing inside it. Whatever you meant to send, someone on the road has it now.
Your letter came to me opened and empty. If you sent something with it, the road has taken it.
Your letter arrived slit open and empty. You should choose your couriers better.

tiresome.t: Letter upon letter from you this season, and now a favour besides. Let me draw breath before I answer that.
You write often, {sir}, and now you ask. I am not a well to be drawn on every week.
I am sorry. You have written so often lately, and I have nothing more to give just now.
So many letters this season, and now a request. We will consider it when the season turns.

warm_gold.t: You asked, and I would be a poor friend to refuse. {replyGold} gold comes with this letter.
Our treasurer has been told to send you {replyGold} gold. Spend it well, and remember the hand that gave it.
I send {replyGold} gold — all I could spare, and I am glad to spare it.
{replyGold} gold rides back with this letter. Don't thank me; you'd have done the same.
You shall have {replyGold} gold from our coffers, sent with our good will, which is worth rather more.
Here is {replyGold} gold, wrapped in a rag so the rider won't hear it chink.

warm_word.t: The treasury is bare just now — I will not pretend otherwise — but you have my word, and I will speak well of you at court.
We will put in a good word for you in {realm}, where our word is listened to.
Our books are full, our coffers less so; but your name will be spoken well of at every counting-table in {realm}.

warm_intel.t: You asked what is said here, so here it is, plainly: {intel}

come.t: You want me back? Then I will come, if you still want me when you see my face.
I have thought of little else since I left. Say the word and I ride.
I'll come. Have someone sharpen my good blade, it's gone dull from idleness.

come_gov.t: I will hand over the keys of {town} and come, if you truly want me at your side again.
Governing {town} has taught me I'd rather be on the road with you. Say the word and the keys go to the reeve.

cool.t: I regret that I cannot help you at present.
We are unable to oblige you in this.
I wish I could help. I can't. I'm sorry.
You ask a great deal on a short acquaintance.
Not this time.
I don't think I'll come back. Not yet. Perhaps not at all.

hostile.t: I am astonished that you would ask anything of me.
You ask a favour of me? After everything? No.
Come back to you? I'd sooner swim home through a winter river.

warm_pact.t: Your proposal of friendship pleases us. Let it be sealed, and let {realm} know you for a friend.
A pact between us would serve us both, and we are not too proud to say so. Send your seal.
Your offer of friendship is the most welcome thing to come by courier this season. We accept it gladly; it wants only your seal.

warm_alliance.t: An alliance between our crowns? We have thought the same. Seal it, and {realm} stands with you.
Our council has debated your proposal and found it good. Let our realms be allies; we wait only for your seal.

warm_truce.t: A truce, then. Our Houses have bled each other long enough. Put your seal to it and I will put mine.
I did not expect to agree with you about anything. I agree to a truce.

warm_marry.t: Yes. Yes, a hundred times. I have read your letter until the ink smudged. Send for me, or come, and let the banns be read.
I will marry you. I wrote it three times before I could make my hand steady enough.

warm_partner.t: We have read your proposal at the counting-table and found the sums good. A partnership, then, if you will seal it.
Rivals make the best partners: they already know where to look. We accept, if you will put your seal to it.

cool.t: We will think on your proposal — which is to say, not now.
Your proposal is noted. The time is not right.
I am touched, truly. But I cannot answer yes, not yet.
We are flattered, but our ledgers say no.

hostile.t: Your proposal was read out at table, and laughed at. I thought you should know.
A truce? Pay what you owe in blood and we will talk of truces.
Friendship with you would be a stain on {realm}.

warm.t: Your apology is accepted. Let what is past stay there.
It takes a good heart to write such a letter. I forgive you, and I will not throw it at you again.
Apology accepted. Don't make me need another.
We accept your apology, and will see whether your deeds keep pace with your ink.

cool.t: Your apology is noted. The wound is not healed.
Words are a beginning. Only a beginning.
I have read your apology. I am trying.

hostile.t: I do not forgive so easily, nor so cheaply as a letter.
An apology from you is worth the paper, and you sent poor paper.

puzzled.t: Your apology puzzles me: I can think of nothing that needs forgiving.
An apology? Whatever for? There was nothing to forgive. Are you quite well?
We know of no offence. If there is one we have not heard of, perhaps it is better left so.
You apologise, but for what? Whatever it was, I never noticed it.
Your apology came. I searched my memory and found no wrong in it.
An apology? I have nothing against you — or nothing yet.
There is nothing between us that needs mending. Put your mind at rest.

paid.t: We would rather have peace than be right. {replyGold} gold comes with this letter; leave us be.
Here — {replyGold} gold. It is what I have. Please, leave my family out of it.
{replyGold} gold, as you demand. Do not think this is the end of it.

cool.t: We refuse your demand. You may do as you think best; so shall we.
No.

hostile.t: You threaten me? Come and try. My people know the roads to {town} better than you do.
Your threat has been read out in our hall, and every sword in it has answered.
I will give you nothing, and I will tell everyone who will listen what kind of letters you write.
Threats are a coward's ink. Write another and I will answer it with steel.
I have taken your letter to the reeve, and the priest has seen it too. Don't write to us again.

warm.t: Your letter is under my pillow, and I am not ashamed to say it.
I have read your letter so often I could say it back to you. You say such things — say them again soon.
I keep your letter where I can touch it. I needn't tell you more than that.
There is no one in the world who writes as you do, and I would not want there to be.
I prayed for you at the shrine this morning, and came home to find your letter. The gods are kind.

cool.t: Your letter touched me. I must be careful in what I answer.
You write very sweetly. I don't know what to write back, so I will say only: thank you.
Such words should not come by courier. People talk.

free.t: We hold no grudge worth a child. {child} is already on the road home, with an escort of our own.
Your letter shamed us a little, as it was meant to. {child} rides home today, and our good will rides too.

price.t: {child} is well, and well kept. The price of {child}'s freedom is {amount} gold, paid to our treasury.
We are not unreasonable. {amount} gold, and {child} comes home.
{child} eats at our table and wants for nothing — but we are not a charity. {amount} gold.

gone.t: {child} is no longer held here. You are writing to the wrong court.

warm.t: Your warning about {enemy} is taken to heart. Our captains will look to the borders.
Your word on {enemy} came none too soon. We are in your debt.
A true friend warns before the blow falls. What you tell of {enemy} has gone straight to our marshal.
What you write of {enemy} squares with what our own spies say. We shall not ask how you know it.

cool.t: We thank you for your warning about {enemy}, though we knew most of it.
{enemy}'s strength is no secret to us. Still, we thank you.
Thank you for the warning. I had heard most of it already, but it is good to know you think of me.
Your warning came. Most of it was old news here, but I am grateful all the same.

hostile.t: We wonder why you trouble to warn us of {enemy}, and what you hope to gain from our fear.
A warning from you smells of a trap. We will watch {enemy} — and you.
I don't need your warnings.

gov.t: Your warning came. I have doubled the watch on the walls of {town}, and the gate shuts at dusk now.
Heard and heeded. The watch at {town} walks in pairs now, and I sleep in my boots.

road.t: Thank you for the warning. I keep to the safer roads now, and keep my knife handy.
You fret like an old hen, but I'll heed you. The safe roads it is.

war.t: The war with {enemy} is all anyone talks of here.
Everyone at {town} talks of the war with {enemy}; we pray it keeps its distance.
{realm} is at war with {enemy}, and {town} feels it in every market.
There is war with {enemy}. Men talk big in the tavern and quiet at home.

war_still.t: The war with {enemy} goes on, and no one here sees the end of it.
Still the war with {enemy}. I am tired of writing that word.

war_over.t: You will be glad to hear the war with {enemy} is over, or over for now.
There is peace with {enemy} at last; I wrote to you of that war, and now I can write that it is done.

lord_war.t: We are at war with {enemy}, as you will know; our captains are in the field and our treasury feels every day of it.
{enemy} tests our borders, and we test their patience. It will end when one of us tires.
The war with {enemy} weighs on us; I have not slept a full night since it began.

lord_war_still.t: Our war with {enemy} goes on, as it did when last I wrote.

lord_war_over.t: Our war with {enemy}, of which I wrote, is ended. We are at peace with them, for what peace is worth.

siege.t: There is a siege at {siegeTown}; we hear the news of it every day, none of it good.
All eyes here are on {siegeTown} and its walls.

siege_still.t: {siegeTown} is still besieged. Every rider brings the same news.

siege_over.t: The siege at {siegeTown} is lifted, one way or another. The road there is open again.

ev_plague.t: There is plague in these parts. We keep our doors shut and burn rosemary, and pray.
The plague has come near {town}. We bar the gates to strangers and trust the physicians as little as we must.
Plague. I will not write more of it than that word; you know what it means.
The gods have sent plague among us. The priests say it is our sins; I say it is the rats.

ev_plague_still.t: The plague is still among us. We have buried more since I last wrote.

ev_plague_over.t: The plague I wrote of has passed us by at last. The bells rang for a whole morning.

ev_famine.t: There is famine here. The children are thin and the old ones give their bread away.
Famine grips the country about {town}; our granaries are open and still it is not enough.

ev_famine_still.t: The famine goes on. I will not pretend otherwise.

ev_famine_over.t: The hunger I wrote of has eased. There is bread on the tables again.

ev_drought.t: No rain for weeks. The wells are low and the fields crack.
The drought holds; the river is a stripe of mud.

ev_flood.t: The river came over its banks and half the low fields are under water.

ev_blizzard.t: The snow came down for three days together and the roads are buried.
We are snowed in. I write by the fire with my feet in a basket of straw.

ev_bandit_uprising.t: Bandits are bold everywhere this season; no cart goes out without a guard.

ev_monster_sighting.t: There is talk of a beast in the country about {town}. The shepherds bring the flocks in early.

ev_festival.t: It is festival time here: music in the square every night and no work done in the mornings.
The festival keeps the whole town awake. I have danced more this week than in a year.

ev_comet_sighting.t: A comet hangs over us at night. The priests argue over what it means; the children just stare.
There is a comet in the sky. Some say it is a sign; I say it is a comet.
A comet burns over {town}. The priests say it is a sign, and I fear they are right.

ev_eclipse.t: The sun went dark at noon a few days since. The dogs howled and old women wept.

ev_refugee_wave.t: People are coming through {town} with their lives on their backs, fleeing somewhere worse.

ev_rebellion.t: There is rebellion in the realm. Nobody knows whom to trust.

ev_religious_schism.t: The priests here are at each other's throats over a point of doctrine. The faithful don't know which way to bow.
There is schism in the faith; it grieves me more than I can say.

ev_gold_rush.t: Gold has been found in the hills, and every fool with a shovel is off to dig.

ev_market_crash.t: The markets have crashed; merchants who were rich last month are selling their furniture.

ev_trade_boom.t: Trade is booming; the wharves and markets have never been so busy.

ev_bountiful_harvest.t: The harvest is the best anyone remembers; the barns are bursting.

ev_earthquake.t: The ground shook here a few days ago; there are cracks in the chapel wall you could put your hand in.

ev_pirate_surge.t: Pirates are thick on the coast; ships come in late or not at all.

outlaws.t: The outlaws of {lair} are bold this season; {leader}'s men take carts on the road to {town} in broad day.
Nobody goes far from {town} after dark — {lair} is too close, and {leader} too bold.
{leader} and his rabble at {lair} need hanging, and nobody in {town} has the rope.

outlaws_still.t: {leader}'s outlaws at {lair} are still a plague on our roads.
{leader} still holds {lair}, and the carters still go round by the long road.
Nobody has rid us of {lair} yet. The reeve talks; {leader} rides.
We still bar the doors at night for fear of {leader}'s men.

outlaws_over.t: The outlaws of {lair} I wrote you of are broken — the roads about {town} are quiet again.

dearth.t: {good} is short at {town}; there is little to be had in the market, and that little is dear.
We cannot get {good} for love nor money in {town}.
The market at {town} is bare of {good}, and my stewards tell me the price climbs every week.
No {good} to be had at {town}. The traders say it will come; the traders always say that.
There's no {good} in {town} worth the name, and what there is costs the earth.

dearth_still.t: There is still no {good} to be had at {town}.
{good} is as scarce at {town} as when I last wrote — scarcer, if anything.
Still no {good} at {town}. We have learned to do without, more or less.
{good} is no easier to come by at {town} than when I last wrote.

dearth_over.t: You will be glad to know there is {good} in the market again at {town}, and at a price a body can pay.
The {good} came back to the market at {town} at last — the shortage I wrote of is over.
We have {good} again at {town}. You never know how much you miss a thing.

glut.t: There is more {good} at {town} than anyone can sell; the traders practically beg in the street.
{good} is a drug on the market at {town} just now — if you have any to sell, don't bring it here.
You can't give {good} away at {town} this season.
{town} is drowning in {good}; the price has fallen through the floor.

dear_food.t: Bread costs {pct} in the hundred more than it did in the {since}, and wages are what they were.
Food at {town} is dearer by {pct} in the hundred since the {since}; the poor feel it first.
Everything to eat costs more — {pct} in the hundred more than in the {since}, the baker's wife says, and she would know.

cheap_food.t: Bread is cheap here this season, which is a mercy.

inflation.t: Everything costs more at {town} — {pct} in the hundred since the {since}, and nobody can say why.

engrossing.t: The grain dealers at {town} have their lofts full and their doors shut, waiting for the price to climb.
The grain is in the dealers' lofts at {town}, and they will not sell. It is a sin, I say.

harvest_failing.t: The crops look poorly about {town}; the old men shake their heads at the fields.
The harvest about {town} is failing; we shall be buying grain before the winter is out.

harvest_failing_still.t: The harvest is no better than I wrote. We shall be hungry by spring.

harvest_failing_over.t: The harvest came in better than we feared, after all I wrote.

harvest_bumper.t: The fields about {town} look fit to burst; it will be a fine harvest.

harvest_poor.t: The harvest was poor here, and everyone knows it.

harvest_plenty.t: The harvest was a good one, and the barns are full.

money_levy.t: The crown has laid a war levy on us, and the tax men are at every door.

money_debased.t: The new coin is half copper; the merchants weigh every penny and trust none.
The coin is clipped and debased; you can bend a penny in your teeth.

money_heavy_taxes.t: The taxes are heavy this year, and heavier on those who can least pay.

money_army_unpaid.t: The soldiers have not been paid in weeks, and an unpaid soldier is a dangerous thing.

money_tax_revolt.t: There was trouble at {town} over the taxes — stones thrown at the collector, and worse.

money_coin_short.t: There is no coin about; half the market here is done in barter.

money_default.t: The crown cannot pay its debts, they say. The bankers are very quiet.

labour_strike.t: The workers at {town} have downed tools and nothing is getting made.

labour_idle.t: There are too many hands and not enough work at {town}; men stand in the square waiting to be hired.

labour_refugees.t: {town} is full of people who fled their homes; they sleep in the church porch.

labour_hardship.t: Times are hard for working folk at {town}. Many go without.

labour_boom.t: There is work for anyone who wants it at {town}; folk are coming in from the villages.

strike.t: The {guild} at {town} are on strike, and there is no {good} to be had until they settle.

strike_over.t: The {guild} have gone back to work at {town}.

road_pass_closed.t: The pass is snowed shut, so your next letter may be slow.

road_flood.t: The roads out of {town} are under water in places; the post is late.

road_ruined.t: The road to {town} is all holes and ruin; a cart broke its axle by my door last week.

road_mud.t: The roads are deep in spring mud; it is a wonder your letter came at all.

road_washed_out.t: The ford below {town} is washed out; the carts go the long way round.

road_highway.t: The new highway makes the ride from {town} a joy; your letters come quicker for it.

road_canal.t: The barges on the canal bring all sorts to {town} now.

road_works.t: They are building a new road near {town}, and every idle man has found work on it.

new_ruler.t: We have a new ruler: {ruler}, now that {oldRuler} is gone. Nobody knows yet what to make of it.
{oldRuler} is dead and {ruler} sits the throne. The criers have been hoarse for a week.

revolt.t: There is revolt in {realm}, and the roads are not safe for anyone wearing the crown's colours.

herald.t: The criers came through {town} with news: {text}
You will have heard it, but here they cried it in the square: {text}

scandal.t: The talk at {town} is all of {subject}: "{taleQ}" I don't know if it is true; I only tell you what is said.
At {town} they are saying of {subject}: "{taleQ}" I set no store by it, but you should know what is said.
Here is a thing they whisper about {subject} — and I only say what they say: "{taleQ}"
Every tavern in {town} has a tale of {subject}: "{taleQ}" People will believe anything with a drink in them.
They tell a story of {subject} at {town}, and tell it often: "{taleQ}"

deed_duel_won.t: Even here we heard how you won your duel {atPlace}. The young men talk of nothing else.
Word came of your duel {atPlace}. I am glad you are alive to read this.

deed_beast_slain.t: They say at {town} that you slew a beast {nearPlace}. I said I knew you, and nobody believed me.

deed_feast_given.t: We heard of your feast {atPlace}; they say the wine ran till dawn.

deed_famine_dole.t: Word reached {town} of the bread you gave out {atPlace}. That is a thing people remember.
People here speak well of you for the bread you gave out {atPlace}. Don't let it go to your head.

deed_pilgrimage_made.t: They say you made a pilgrimage {toPlace}. The gods will remember it.

deed_pardon.t: We heard you showed mercy {atPlace}. Mercy is talked of more than cruelty, whatever men think.

deed_wilds_rescue.t: The tale of how you brought someone out of the wilds {nearPlace} has reached even {town}.

deed_sack.t: We have heard what was done {atPlace}, and by whose order.
They speak of {place} here in low voices, and of you in lower ones.

deed_murder.t: There is talk here of a killing {atPlace}, and your name is in it. I hope it is a lie.
They say at {town} that you have blood on your hands from {place}. I believe it.

deed_theft.t: There is talk at {town} of a theft {atPlace}, and your name comes up. I said nothing.
Thief. They know your name in {town} now.

deed_assault.t: They say at {town} you beat a man {atPlace}. I hope he had it coming.
Word of what you did {atPlace} has reached {town}. Nobody here is surprised.

deed_affair.t: There is talk here — idle talk, I hope — of you and {victim}. Be careful what you put in letters.
All {town} knows about you and {victim}. So does everyone who matters.

fashion.t: The fashion at court is {fashion}, and every merchant in {place} is selling {goods} at twice the price.

season_spring.t: Spring has come; the lambs are out and the roads are mud.
The spring here is late and cold, and the blossom is only just showing.
The fields are being ploughed and the ditches cleared; spring keeps everyone busy.

season_summer.t: It is high summer; the days are long and the flies are worse.
Summer is here, and the court is restless as it always is in the heat.
The hay is in, or most of it. My arms ache from the scything.

season_autumn.t: The leaves are turning and the swallows have gone; there is woodsmoke on the air every evening.
Autumn is here; we are getting the harvest in and the wood stacked.
It is autumn, and the court talks of nothing but the hunting.

season_winter.t: It is bitter here; the water froze in the jug last night.
Winter has us shut indoors with the fire and each other's tempers.
Winter is upon us, and our halls are cold however many logs we burn.

ruler_ill.t: I write this from my bed. The physicians bleed me and frown, and I frown back.
We have been unwell this past while; our physicians are hopeful, which is what physicians are paid to be.
I have been ill, and am not yet well. Pray for me, if you pray.

ruler_ill_still.t: I am still abed, as when I last wrote; the physicians promise much and do little.

ruler_ill_over.t: You will be glad to know the fever I wrote of has left me. I rode out yesterday for the first time in weeks.
We are recovered from the illness of which we wrote, the gods be thanked.

spouse_ill.t: My consort {spouse} has been ill these past weeks; I sit with {spouse} in the evenings.

lord_birth.t: We have been blessed with a {childWord}, {child}, born this season. The bells have not stopped.
I have a new {childWord}: {child}. Small, loud, and already the master of the household.

lord_heir.t: My {childWord} {child} is {age} now and rides better than I ever did.
{child}, my {childWord}, is {age}, and has begun to sit in council with me. Heaven help the council.

lord_new.t: You will know {oldRuler} is dead, and the crown of {realm} has come to me. It is heavier than it looks.
Since the death of {oldRuler} the governance of {realm} is in our hands, and we mean to keep it well.

rival_child.t: My {childWord} {child} is {age} now, and asks about your House more than I would like.
{child}, my {childWord}, turns {age} this year. Children grow; feuds, it seems, do not.

rival_errand.t: I ride for {place} within the week, on business you will hear of soon enough.
My people are bound for {place}. Make of that what you will.

spouse_kid.t: {child} asks for you every night, and every night I say soon.
{child} is {age} now and {he} has your temper, I am sorry to say.
{child} wanted to write to you too; I have folded {his} letter inside mine. It is mostly drawings of horses.
{child} is well and growing, and keeps asking when you will come home.

spouse_missing.t: The bed is too wide without you.
I keep your place at the table. The servants think me foolish.
Come home when you can. I am not asking, I am telling.
I light a candle for you every evening.

child_held.t: They are courteous to me here in {realm}, but I see the guards at my door, and they see me.

child_spouse.t: {spouse} is kind to me, and I am learning to be kind back.

governing.t: {town} keeps me busy from first light: petitions, quarrels, the watch, the tolls. I never knew how much paper a town eats.
Governing {town} is a slower kind of fighting. I am learning it.

life_wed.t: I have news: I am married! {name} and I were wed this season.
I wed {first} this season. You would like {first}, I think.

life_courting.t: I have been walking out with {name}. There, I have told someone.
I am courting {first}, and my heart is light as a feather. Don't laugh.
I'm courting {first}. That's all I'll say.
{first} and I keep company now, with my family's blessing, God willing.

life_betrothed.t: I am to be married! {name} asked, and I said yes.
{first} and I are promised. Will you come to the wedding? Say you will.
I'm getting wed. {first}. The banns are read.

life_heartbroken.t: {first} and I are no more. I would rather not write of it.
My heart is broken, and {first} broke it. I shall mend, they say.
{first} and I are done. Good riddance.

life_birth.t: We have a little {childWord}, {child}, born this season. Loud as a crow and twice as hungry.
The gods sent us a {childWord} this season; we named the child {child}.

widowed.t: I must tell you my {spouseWord} {name} is dead — {cause}. The house is very quiet.
{name} is gone. {cause}. I don't know what else to write.

widowed_still.t: I still set two cups on the table some mornings, from habit.

widowed_over.t: The grief I wrote you of is lighter now. Not gone, but lighter.

life_child_died.t: We lost our {childWord} {name} — {cause}. I cannot write more of it.

life_parent_died.t: My {parentWord} {name} passed this season. It was time, they say. It never feels like time.

life_kid_left.t: Our {name} has gone off to {to}. The house feels bigger and emptier.
{name} left for {to}. Young folk always think the grass is greener.

life_retired.t: I have given up the work of a {work}; my back would not have it any longer.

sick.t: I write this from my bed. I have {illness}, and the herbalist frowns when she thinks I'm not looking.
Forgive the hand: I am down with {illness}. It will pass, God willing.
I've {illness}. Don't fuss. I've had worse.

sick_still.t: I am still abed with that sickness I wrote of.

sick_over.t: I am up and about again after {illness}. Thin as a rake, but alive.

kin_sick.t: My {kin} {name} is down with {illness}, and I sit up with them every night.
Pray for my {kin} {name}. It is {illness}, and a bad one.

kin_sick_still.t: {name} is no better yet. We wait.

kin_sick_over.t: The sickness I wrote of has left our house at last.

town_sick.t: There is {illness} going round the town. We keep the children in.
Sickness has come to us: {illness}. The priest is out every day, and the sexton too.
We have {illness} in the town. Some say it came with the carters. Come no nearer than you must.

town_sick_still.t: The sickness is still in the town. More houses shut every week.

town_sick_over.t: The sickness that was in the town has passed. We have our dead to mourn, but the bells ring for the living again.

hurt.t: I am still mending from a beating — it will heal, the wise-woman says.
I have been laid up hurt. Don't fuss; it is mending.

hurt_still.t: I am still not right from that beating I wrote of.

hurt_over.t: I am mended now, thank you for asking — or for not asking.

family_kid.t: My {childWord} {child} is {age} now and into everything.
{child} is {age} and asks who writes me letters. I said a friend.

family_grown.t: My {childWord} {child} is grown, and a {work} now.
{child} is a {work} now, and thinks they know everything.

neighbour.t: You'll remember the folk here, maybe. {text}.

neighbour_love.t: And here is a bit of gossip for you. {text}.

request_food.t: I would not ask if it were not hard, but we are short of {good} here. If you could send {qty} {good} — or {gold} gold to buy it, if you have it to spare — we would bless your name.
I have a thing to ask. {good} is not to be had at {town}. Could you send {qty}? Or {gold} gold, and we will find some.
Forgive me for asking. We are hungry here, and there is no {good}. {qty} {good}, or {gold} gold — anything would help.
{town} is short of {good}. If you could spare {qty}, or {gold} gold towards it, the town would remember who helped.
I hate to ask. But there is no {good} at {town}, and the children ask for it. {qty} {good} would do, or {gold} gold.
The larder is low — no {good} in {town} for any money. If you could send {qty}, or {gold} gold, I would be easier.

invite_visit.t: Come and see us at {town} if your road brings you near, before {deadline}. There will be a bed for you, and supper.
You must come to {town} — truly, I mean it. Before {deadline}, if you can.
If you are near {town} before {deadline}, come by. I'll not ask twice.
Come home to {town} before {deadline}, if you can. I would like to see your face.

invite_feast.t: You will have a letter from our steward bidding you to our table; come, and be seen to come.
My steward writes separately about a feast. Do come — the company is dull without enemies or friends, and you may be either.

tip_agent.t: A word to you, quietly: {agent}, the {role} here, has been drinking with men in the colours of {rival}, and asks a great many questions about your affairs.
I should not say this, but you have been kind to me. Watch {agent}, the {role}. Money from {rival} goes into that purse.
Watch {agent}, the {role} at {town}. {rival} pays for something, and it isn't the ale.

tip_lair.t: If you ride this way, beware the country near {where}: {leader}'s outlaws keep {lair} there, and they are not gentle with travellers.
The outlaws who trouble us have their hole at {lair}, near {where} — {leader} leads them. I tell you so that you will know the road.

secret_true.t: One thing more, for your eyes only: the tale they tell of {subject} is true. I have it from one who knows. Burn this.
You will have heard what they say of {subject}. I will tell you plainly: it is true. Keep it close.

secret_false.t: And this, between ourselves: what they say of {subject} is a lie, and I know who began it. Don't be taken in.
Do not believe what is said of {subject}. It is false, and I know it for certain.

enclose_coin.t: I put {coin} in with this. Don't argue; it's yours.
There are {coin} in the fold of this letter, for your road. It is not much.

enclose_goods.t: I send {goodsLine} with the rider, bought in the market here — something from {town} to remember us by.
The rider carries {goodsLine} from {town}. Don't say I never gave you anything.

enclose_token.t: Inside I have put {token}. You will know why.
Inside is {token}. Keep it near you.
There is {token} in with this. Don't laugh.

spring: a sprig of blossom, a little crushed
summer: a dried rose, a little crushed
autumn: a red leaf from the garden
any: a lock of hair, tied with red thread
a little knot of plaited grass
kid: a drawing by {child} of a horse — or possibly a dog
a little carved horse {child} made for you

closings.t: Given under our hand and seal at {town}.
With every good wish for your health and your House,
May the gods keep you, as we pray they will.
Ever your friend, whatever the world says,
We remain, as ever, watchful of our friends,
With the honour you have earned of us, and no more,
With all my heart, and more than this paper holds,

clerk.t: Written fair by a clerk of the chancery, and sealed with the seal of {realm}.
A clerk's careful hand, under the great seal of {realm}.
Put into your own tongue by a clerk of the chancery of {realm}, and sealed with its seal.
A clerk's careful hand, in your own tongue, under the great seal of {realm}.
Under the seal of {realm} — and in the court's own tongue: nobody troubled to put it into yours.
In a clerk's hand, on the counting-house's paper.

scribe.t: Set down by {scribe} of {town} for {writer}, who cannot write.
Written by {scribe} at {town}, word for word as {first} said it.

mouth.t: No letter came: a carter from {town} brought word from {writer} by mouth, and gave it like this.
A pedlar out of {town} carried word from {writer}, who cannot write, and repeated it as best he could.

rival.t: In a secretary's hand, put into your tongue, under the seal of {sigHouse}.
Written in the tongue of {realm}, and sealed with {sigHouse}'s seal. No courtesy of translation.

own.t: In {first}'s own hand, a little blotted.

ps.t: Forgive the blots; the ink is poor and so is my hand.
Burn this when you have read it. Or don't — I don't suppose it matters.
I have said a prayer for your road.
Give my regards to whoever is fool enough to ride with you.
The rider ate all our bread. Tip him less next time.
I meant to write more, but the candle is out.
Mind your health; you never do.
I nearly forgot — the dog had pups.
Do not trust the courier from the south road; he reads what he carries.
Excuse the brevity; there is a petitioner at the door.
The seal is a new one; the old cracked in the cold.
The roof leaks again. I mention it only so you know I am not complaining about anything else.
Burn the candle at both ends if you must, but sleep sometimes.
There is a cough going round {town}; mind yourself if you pass through.

openings.t: I have not heard from you in a while, so I write first.
No letter from you, so here is one from me.
I take up my pen without waiting for yours.
{scribe} has kindly agreed to write this for me.
A rider is going your way, so I send this with him.
I write because there is news, and you should have it from a friend.
It has been too long since we wrote, so I am writing.
The carrier leaves at first light, and I would not let him go empty-handed.
We write unbidden, which we do not often do.

condolence_spouse.t: I heard of {dead}'s death and could not let it pass without a word. I am so sorry.
We have learned with great sorrow of the death of {dead}. Our thoughts are with your House.
{dead} is gone, and I grieve with you. The gods keep {dead} now.
{dead} was a good soul. I don't know what else to say, except that I am here if you need me.

condolence_child.t: I have heard about {dead}. There are no words for it, so I will not pretend to have any. I am sorry.
We learn with deep sorrow of the loss of your {deadWord} {dead}. No crown or House is proof against such grief.
{dead}. I lit a candle the hour I heard. The gods hold {dead} gently now.
I heard about {dead}. I am crying as I write this.

congrats_birth.t: I hear you have a new {childWord}, {child}! A thousand blessings on the little one.
We have heard of the birth of {child} to your House, and send our congratulations.
A {childWord}! {child}! Kiss the little one for me.
Heard about {child}. Good. May the child have your luck and none of your enemies.

congrats_wed.t: I hear you are married to {spouse}! I am so glad for you.
We have heard of your marriage to {spouse}, and wish you both every joy.
Married! To {spouse}! I always said you would be, and nobody believed me.

congrats_crown.t: We have heard that {yourRealm} is yours. We salute a fellow crown.
A crown! I knew you when you had holes in your boots.
The crown of {yourRealm}, they say. May you wear it better than most.

grateful.t: I am sixteen now, and done with my schooling, and I write this in my own hand, which I could never have done without you.
You paid for my letters when no one else would. Here is the first letter I ever wrote, and it is to you.
I can read and write now. Thank you. If ever you need someone, send for me.
God bless you for my schooling. I pray for you every holy day.

news.t: Nothing has happened that you need to act upon; I only wanted you to know how things stand with us.
Nothing much has happened here, but I said I would write, so I am writing.
It has been a while, and I wanted you to know how we are getting on.
There is no great news, only the small kind — but you always said you liked the small kind.
I hope you don't mind my writing without being written to.
Our affairs leave a moment's leisure, and we spend it on you.
I prayed for you at the evening bell, and it put me in mind to write.
The house is asleep and I am writing to you by the last of the candle.
Quiet here. Too quiet. So I am writing to you instead of sharpening things.
I thought you would want the news, such as it is.
We thought it right to keep you informed of affairs in {realm}.

request.t: I write to ask a thing of you, and I would not, if I had anyone else to ask.

missing.t: You have been gone a long while. I am not complaining. I am only telling you.
I miss you. There, I have written it.
It is very quiet here without you.

deed.t: I had to write when I heard the news of you.
Word of you has reached us, and I could not keep my pen still.
We hear of you even here.
